kinds.d: Lighter carried on the person, from windproof wick lighters to disposable butane ones.

x.d: Wick-and-naphtha windproof lighter first made in early 1933 by George Blaisdell, inspired by an Austrian IMCO lighter; patent 1936; lifetime guarantee.

v.d: Dots from 1955, later letter and numeral codes

x.d: One-hand automatic lighter lighting and extinguishing with a single push; sold in 1927 as the Ronson De-Light.
One of the first butane gas lighters; design stayed largely unchanged and appeared with James Bond.
Paris house whose first serially produced lighter, in 1941, was made of aluminium.
American lighter house founded by Julius Lowenthal.
Disposable butane lighter made by Société Bic since 1973; over 30 billion sold by February 2024.
Refillable butane lighter designed by Enric Sardà, made by Flamagas (founded 1959) in Barcelona.

kinds.d: Lighter made for lighting cigars, usually a jet or torch flame.
Lighter with a side flame for lighting a pipe bowl.
Lighter made to stand on a table.

x.d: Table lighter made from the early 1930s, often in Art Deco designs.

kinds.d: Lighter that makes an electric arc (plasma) or heats an element, rechargeable by USB, with no fuel or flint.
Consumables for lighters: naphtha (Zippo) and butane fuel, ferrocerium flints and wicks.

brands.d: Founded by George Blaisdell in Bradford, Pennsylvania; owns Ronson in North America since 2010.
Began as Art Metal Works in Newark; bankrupt 2010, Zippo bought the North American marks.
Founded by Julius Lowenthal; now New York based.
Paris house founded by Simon Tissot-Dupont; lighters from 1941.
London house; butane lighter mid-1950s; lighters were about 75% of sales by 1975.
Maker of the disposable Bic lighter, introduced 1973.
Refillable butane lighter of Flamagas, founded 1959.

notes: Dunhill Rollagas/Unique/Aquarium, Ligne 2, Maxijet, Varaflame, Queen Anne, IMCO, Cricket not on retrieved pages; omitted. Colibri cigar-lighter list trimmed to one model; Aura, Ascari etc dropped. Colibri also kept in table/pipe lighters via old models.
